Policies that matter

  • Cancellation: Please provide 48-hour notice. Missed sessions or late cancellations may incur a fee of half the session rate.
  • Payments: Card on file or prepayment for blocks. Monthly plan billed at start of cycle.
  • Confidentiality & privacy: Sessions are private and protected; I follow professional confidentiality rules. For specifics, see the intake packet.

Myth vs. Practical View

Myth: Therapy is only for crises.
Truth: Therapy often works best as a steady, preventive practice — a place to build skills and process transitions before they become emergencies.

A brief example

Client A sought help for burnout. We began weekly sessions, shifted to biweekly after three months, and then transitioned to a membership plan focused on relapse prevention and skill refreshers. Financing the block sessions gave predictability and reduced the cognitive load of scheduling.

Quick answers

How does sliding scale work?
I reserve a small number of reduced-fee slots. Availability is discussed at intake and requires brief verification.
Do you accept insurance?
I do not bill insurance directly but provide superbills for clients who seek out-of-network reimbursement.
Is there a cancellation fee?
Yes, with exceptions during documented emergencies. I aim for transparent, predictable policies.
Schedule a time

Scope & boundaries: I provide psychotherapy for adults with anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship stress, life transitions and burnout. I do not provide emergency services; if you are in crisis, call local emergency services or a crisis line immediately.

Practical answers about process, scope, and safety

Below are common questions clients ask before they begin. If you don't see an answer, reach out — I'm glad to clarify.

Journey & methods

Which therapeutic approaches do you use?
I draw from evidence-informed methods—trauma-informed cognitive-behavioral strategies, somatic awareness, and interpersonal frameworks—selected collaboratively to fit your goals.
How long does therapy usually take?
There's no fixed timeline. Some people find relief in short-term focused work (6–12 sessions); others benefit from longer-term exploration. We set measurable goals and periodically review progress.
Are sessions confidential?
Yes: clinical notes and conversations are confidential within professional limits. Exceptions include imminent risk of harm, court orders, or mandated reporting. A full privacy statement is included in the intake materials.
What should I expect at intake?
The first appointment combines clinical history, goal-setting, and practical orientation (scheduling, fees, emergency plans). It is an opportunity both to assess fit and to begin work.
What if I am in crisis?
I do not provide crisis services. If you are in immediate danger, please call local emergency services or a crisis hotline. If you are suicidal or feel unsafe, contact 988 (U.S.) or your local emergency number.
Do you work with couples or families?
My primary practice focuses on individual adult psychotherapy. For couples or family therapy I may offer referrals or limited co-therapy options depending on training and fit.

Measuring progress: what I track

We use symptom tracking, goal review, and periodic check-ins about life functioning. If something isn't moving, we adapt the plan. Therapy is iterative and data-informed rather than one-size-fits-all.

Common misconceptions clarified

Therapy requires full vulnerability right away. I pace disclosure and skills work to what feels safe and useful.

I will tell you what to do. My role is to guide and teach skills; decisions remain yours.

Core pillars of my work

  • Safety first: practical interventions when distress is high
  • Curiosity: hypothesis-driven exploration
  • Skill-building: concrete practices you can use

Short vignette

A client working with relationship anxiety learned communication scripts alongside somatic regulation—combining skills and reflective work reduced reactivity and improved connection.

Begin intake & scheduling

Ethical note: The information here is educational and not a substitute for emergency care. Confidentiality is honored within legal and ethical limits. If you need immediate help, contact emergency services in your area.

Schedule an initial appointment

A short intake helps us clarify needs, immediate safety, and the best path forward. If you're unsure which option fits, use the notes field below.

You will receive an intake packet and consent forms if we move forward.

Fees: Single sessions, blocks, and membership options are available. I provide superbills for out-of-network reimbursement. For detailed investment options, see the Investments page.

What happens after you request a time

  1. I will review your request and follow up within 48 business hours with available times and intake paperwork.
  2. The intake form covers confidentiality, emergency planning, and questions about goals and history.
  3. We discuss mutual fit; if I am not the best match, I will offer referrals.

Booking — quick FAQs

First appointment: A structured intake and assessment; you can expect some paperwork and our first therapeutic steps.
Telehealth or in-person? Both. Telehealth uses a secure, HIPAA-aligned platform unless otherwise agreed.
How to prepare: Have a quiet private space, a stable internet connection for video, and a list of immediate concerns or questions you want to address.

Therapeutic priorities

My work emphasizes safety, measurable skills, and collaborative problem-solving — a blend of practical tools and reflective inquiry to support meaningful change.

Send a question

Confidentiality: Your information is confidential within professional boundaries. Scope & boundaries: I treat adults for anxiety, trauma, relationship concerns, life transitions, and burnout. I do not provide emergency services; if you are currently in crisis, call emergency services or a crisis hotline.
